Two candidates re-promoted today from the 2026-09-15.json watch pool (daysSinceFirstSeen=1) after fresh full-text credibility verification: 2609.11987 (Harness or Model?) and 2609.12191 (GAUGE).

toolDegradation: Groundlane web_fetch on the raw arXiv HTML list pages (arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new, cs.CL/new) did not render paper titles/authors in markdown/text extraction (only arXiv IDs + pdf/html/other links were returned by the reader); worked around this by (1) confirming the official announcement-batch ID range and date via the list pages, and (2) cross-referencing titles/abstracts for those same IDs via the arXiv Atom export API (export.arxiv.org/api/query) and Groundlane web_search/web_fetch on individual arxiv.org/abs/{id} pages.

arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new could not be fetched in full even at maxBytes=20000000 ('Upstream response exceeds the byte limit'); worked around via a reduced ?skip=0&show=250 query and via targeted arXiv API + web_search discovery instead of enumerating all ~150 cs.AI entries individually.

Semantic Scholar public Graph API (api.semanticscholar.org) returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) for the large majority of per-paper citationCount/venue lookups this run, including for all three selected papers on repeated retries. Citation velocity is reported as 'not retrievable this round, rate-limited' rather than a queried number; this is judged low-impact since all three selected papers are 5-8 day old preprints where citation counts would realistically still be in the low single digits.

Groundlane MCP (web_search/web_fetch) itself was available and used as the primary tool throughout; no fallback beyond Groundlane -> arXiv official API -> Semantic Scholar was needed for paper content. No fallback chain degradation below Groundlane occurred.

candidates.title: GAUGE: When Not to Trust LLM-as-a-Judge in User-Simulated Evaluation of Task-Oriented Agents
candidates.citationVelocity: not retrievable this round (Semantic Scholar API 429); ~6 days since submission
communitySignals: Not found on HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code this round; EMNLP Industry Track acceptance is the primary endorsement
credibilityEvidence: Section 3 (Method/problem formulation): defines ranking validity vs construct validity formally against a non-LLM verifiable reward
Section 4.1: satisfaction-success gap (57.5% false-accept) across 5 rater populations, 2 benchmarks
Section 4.2: ranking robustness (rho=0.94) vs decision-disagreement rate (31% on close pairs)
Section 4.6: explicit negative result (recalibration does not transfer out-of-sample)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: 25 agents x 6 providers x 2 benchmarks x ~3,700 transcripts with 4 parallel scoring signals including a non-LLM verifiable reward; core claims (satisfaction-success gap, ranking vs decision-disagreement) are cross-checked across rater populations and both substrates
reproducibilityEvidence: No public code/data release link found via web_search this round; underlying benchmarks (tau2-bench, SimulatorArena) are public but the authors' audit protocol/transcripts are not confirmed public
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: the two headline numbers (57.5%, 31%) are well replicated across rater populations and benchmarks; the paper itself scopes the calibrate-then-trust remedy's limits (does not transfer across configs)
candidates.primaryLimitation: Calibrated trust region does not transfer across configuration changes (Section 4.6 negative result) — requires re-auditing on every config change rather than a one-time calibration
candidates.presentationReason: method, validity distinctions (ranking vs construct), and negative results are clearly separated and stated

candidates.title: Harness or Model? Isolating the Harness Effect in Agentic Coding with a Contamination-Controlled Private Suite
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (ACM classification tags present, no confirmed acceptance)
candidates.citationVelocity: not retrievable this round (Semantic Scholar API 429); revised version ~8 days since re-submission
candidates.institution: evolutionID GmbH, Germany — solo independent researcher (Mohsen Arjmandi)
communitySignals: Not found on HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code this round
credibilityEvidence: Section 2: 256-task contamination-controlled suite (179 private repo tasks + 77 post-cutoff contest tasks), frozen cutoff registry, runtime drift gate
Section 3: paired same-model harness contrasts, KVM microVM isolation, Docker-isolated grading oracle, 792/800 planned runs graded
Section 4 (per abstract/intro): task-bootstrap 95% CIs for both contrasts, explicit post-hoc flag on the workload-interaction finding
Section 5.1: documented usage-semantics telemetry defect and its correction as a methods contribution
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: the core 'no resolved average harness advantage' claim is well-supported by bootstrap CIs on both contrasts; but the more striking repo-vs-contest interaction is a post-hoc partition the authors themselves flag as needing a designed replication, and the billing-order question is explicitly left unresolved
reproducibilityEvidence: Abstract/intro states: 'We release the orchestrator, grading oracle, reanalysis code and derived aggregates.' Core 256 private tasks intentionally withheld to preserve contamination control.
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: main claim (no stable average advantage) is solid; the two most attention-grabbing sub-findings (interaction effect, billing order) are self-flagged by the authors as unresolved/post-hoc, so article language is scoped down accordingly
candidates.primaryLimitation: Core task suite stays private (no external exact-replication possible); 58 runs on the Anthropic account left no usage record, leaving the billing-order question between harnesses unresolved
candidates.presentationReason: unusually transparent for a solo-authored paper — documents its own prior telemetry defect, amendments log, and explicitly separates confirmed vs post-hoc findings

credibilityEvidence: Section 3 (Method): Continual Search vs Passive Continuation control design, same turn-1 seed for both branches

candidates.primaryLimitation: MegaRCA-Mix is a new 50-trial benchmark built and annotated by the paper's own authors with no external validation; the method can flip correct judge verdicts to incorrect ones on short-trajectory benchmarks
candidates.presentationReason: method, benchmarks, and boundary conditions (where the method does and does not help) are clearly separated

candidates.citationVelocity: not retrievable this round (Semantic Scholar API 429)
candidates.institution: not captured this round (author Andrei Kozyrev, affiliation not stated on abs page)

candidates.reason: Directly on-topic (repository SKILLs for coding agents, relevant to this site's own Agent Skills workflow) and honestly reported, but the authors themselves state the core 4.9pp effect cannot be statistically separated from run-to-run variance at n=3 repositories — the central quantitative claim is explicitly unresolved by the paper's own admission. Compared with the selected trio (GAUGE: ~3,700 transcripts with bootstrap-validated gaps; Harness or Model?: 792 graded runs with task-bootstrap CIs; Continual Search: consistent multi-benchmark gains), the evidence scale and statistical resolving power here are markedly weaker.
